clue.text: 1938 satirical novel, something published in Pravda?

definitions.meaning: Evelyn Waugh's 1938 novel lampooning Fleet Street foreign correspondents
an exclusive news story that a paper such as the Soviet daily Pravda might print first

explanation.surface: A satirical novel of 1938 is wryly likened to something the Soviet party newspaper might run.
explanation.definitionFit: Waugh's comic novel about journalism bears the title of the newspaper word for an exclusive story.

clue.text: Motorway in a bit of French territory

indicators.note: the motorway letter sits within the word for a bit

parts.note: some means a bit, a portion
M is the usual abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: A motorway runs through a small piece of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somme is a French department, an administrative territory named after its river.

clue.text: Perverse bloom, reportedly, of a famously idle man

indicators.note: perverse means contrary or wrong, so the letters of bloom are set the wrong way
reportedly signals that the next word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: the little word of, spoken, sounds like the letters OV

explanation.surface: Someone notorious for laziness is linked with an oddly behaving flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perverse' turns BLOOM into OBLOM; 'reportedly' turns 'of' into its sound, OV.
explanation.definitionFit: Goncharov's novel made its title character a byword for slothful inertia, a man who barely leaves his bed.

clue.text: "Clean your finger, before you my spots" (Benjamin Franklin)

definitions.text: "Clean your finger, before you my spots" (Benjamin Franklin)

parts.words: "Clean your finger, before you my spots" (Benjamin Franklin)
parts.note: a quotation with its key words left out; the solver supplies the gap, which is the act of indicating someone else's flaws

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing words go between 'you' and 'my'. Franklin's maxim warns against criticising others before checking one's own faults.
explanation.definitionFit: The gap in Franklin's proverb takes the phrasal verb for singling out or indicating with a finger.

clue.text: A politician with maturity protecting a monarch's measure of power

indicators.note: to protect is to surround, so the outer letters enclose the monarch

parts.note: MP is Member of Parliament
age means maturity, years of experience
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the usual crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A grown-up politician shields the sovereign's degree of authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical current rating in amps, loosely a measure of how much power a circuit carries.

clue.text: Prince and Pope meeting elevated archdeacon on a TV channel

parts.note: several popes took the name Alexander

indicators.note: in a down entry elevated means raised up, so the abbreviation is read bottom to top

parts.note: Ven, Venerable, is the title abbreviation for an archdeacon
Sky is a British satellite television broadcaster

explanation.surface: A prince and a pope meet a senior cleric on a television network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns VEN into NEV. Sky is a British TV company.
explanation.definitionFit: The thirteenth-century Russian ruler and saint, subject of Eisenstein's film, held the princely title of Novgorod.

clue.text: Awful pun by Sikh poet

indicators.note: awful suggests something mangled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dreadful wordplay joke comes from a Sikh versifier.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia's national poet, author of Eugene Onegin.

clue.text: Comment adversely on amount of water in river

indicators.note: the measure is placed inside the river word

parts.note: rio is Spanish and Portuguese for river, as in Rio Grande
a pint is a measured quantity of liquid

explanation.surface: Someone criticises how much water is flowing in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to attack verbally or criticise harshly.

clue.text: A president, or in our country, a revolutionary victor

indicators.note: the word or is placed within the country abbreviation

parts.note: GB, Great Britain, as seen by a British setter
Che Guevara, the archetypal crossword revolutionary
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A head of state, or a triumphant rebel in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikhail Gorbachev was the first and only executive head of state of the Soviet Union.

clue.text: Espionage manager in London starts on measures about English key operator in Russia

indicators.note: the first letters of the four preceding words are taken
the measure word is placed around the English abbreviation

parts.note: gills are small liquid measures

explanation.surface: A spymaster in London runs a radio operator in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key operator' looks like espionage slang for a radio man; it means a pianist, one who works keys. 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Emil Gilels was a great Soviet pianist, someone who plays the keyboard.

clue.text: City once called Yuriatin a monarch visited in the afternoon

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so the monarch sits within the time abbreviation

parts.note: PM, post meridiem, marks afternoon hours
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A queen pays an afternoon call on a city with a fictional former name.
explanation.walkthrough: Yuriatin is the fictional city in Pasternak's Doctor Zhivago, modelled on a real Urals city.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasternak based his invented Urals town on the real city on the Kama river.

clue.text: 18 short stories include one about 3 -s

parts.note: read 18 as the Russian writer at 18 down and 3 as the number three: one of his tales concerns three holy recluses living on an island

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references are the trick: '18' is the writer at 18 down, and '3' is simply the number, not a clue reference. His story is The Three Hermits.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolstoy's tale tells of three solitary holy men living alone on an island, religious recluses.

clue.text: "A right state" in America …

parts.note: Kansas is a US state

explanation.surface: Something described as a proper state is located in America, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 12 across in surface only; each is solved alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkansas is one of the fifty United States, so it is a state in America.

clue.text: … was subject to poll between detective and lecturer

indicators.note: the poll word is placed between the detective and the lecturer

parts.note: PI, private investigator
a don is a university lecturer
to poll is to vote

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, the state went to the ballot between a sleuth and an academic.
explanation.definitionFit: Hinged on, depended on: a matter that pivots on something is governed by it.

clue.text: Push forward against an entrance

parts.note: to prop something is to lean it against a support
the indefinite article gives A
a gate is a way in

explanation.surface: Someone shoves forward against a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread or promote an idea or plant, advancing it further.

clue.text: A line of darts in crochet

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the word crochet

explanation.surface: A row of tucks appears in a piece of crochet work.
explanation.walkthrough: Darts suggests dressmaking tucks, which crochet supports; it is the pub game, whose throwing line is the oche.
explanation.definitionFit: The oche is the line a player stands behind when throwing in the pub game of darts.

clue.text: Composer of songs reverses run

indicators.note: reverses tells us to write the run word backwards

parts.note: to flow is to run, like water

explanation.surface: A songwriter turns back in a run.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugo Wolf was an Austrian composer famed above all for his lieder, art songs.

clue.text: Good old monarch to see nearly famous jeweller

parts.note: fab, short for fabulous, is old slang for good
ER, Elizabeth Regina

indicators.note: nearly means the final letter is dropped from the word for see

parts.note: to get something is to see it, understand it

explanation.surface: A fine old king goes to view a celebrated maker of gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Carl Faberge made jewelled Easter eggs for the Russian tsars.

clue.text: Russian author revising volume with mentor

indicators.note: revising means reworking the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A Russian writer edits a book with his teacher's help.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikhail Lermontov was a Russian Romantic poet and novelist, author of A Hero of Our Time.

clue.text: Cuts in education announced

indicators.note: announced signals the word is taken as it sounds when said

parts.note: lessons are the units of teaching in education

explanation.surface: Budget reductions in schooling are made public.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen is to reduce, so lessens means cuts down.

clue.text: Variety of food is good in Mediterranean city, I see

indicators.note: the good letter sits inside the city name

parts.note: Oran is a port in Algeria on the Mediterranean
the letter C sounds like see; C is also a common crossword stand-in for the verb

explanation.surface: A diner notices a range of dishes is fine in a southern port.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic produce is a class of food grown without synthetic chemicals.

clue.text: Play about lost tragic Russian writer

indicators.note: the play word wraps around the scrambled letters

parts.note: to toy is to play

indicators.note: tragic suggests something wrecked, so the letters of lost are scrambled

explanation.surface: A drama about a lost, doomed Russian novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' reads as a stage drama but is the verb; 'tragic' gives OLST, which 'about' wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Tolstoy wrote War and Peace and Anna Karenina.

clue.text: Kiss when clutched by naked French communist

indicators.note: clutched by means held inside the outer word

parts.note: bare means naked
buss is an old word for a kiss

explanation.surface: A kiss given while held by a nude French red.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Barbusse was a French novelist and member of the Communist Party.

clue.text: French cigarettes no use for French mathematician

indicators.note: no use says the letters of use are taken out

parts.note: Gauloises are a French cigarette brand

explanation.surface: A French mathematician's cigarettes are found to be useless.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters U, S, E are removed in order from GAULOISES, not as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Evariste Galois was the French mathematician who founded group theory.

clue.text: A fictional prince or god in Italian twice over

indicators.note: the god word is placed inside the Italian abbreviation

parts.note: dio is the Italian word for god

explanation.surface: A storybook prince, or a deity in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice over' says Italian works twice: dio is god in Italian, and IT, Italian, holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dostoevsky's novel calls its hero, Prince Myshkin, by this title.

clue.text: Royal Standard's preceding a Queen

indicators.note: preceding puts the standard word before the queen letter

parts.note: par means a standard, the norm; the 's is just is
R, Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: The royal flag goes before a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal Standard' looks like the flag; the definition is 'Royal', a noun: Catherine Parr, Henry VIII's sixth wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine Parr was a queen consort of England, a member of royalty.

clue.text: Film director's genius seen around a filming location when short of time

indicators.note: seen around says the genius word surrounds the shortened location

parts.note: Einstein is the byword for a genius

indicators.note: short of means the time letter is removed

parts.note: a set is where a film is shot

explanation.surface: A movie director's brilliance shows around a studio stage minus some time.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei Eisenstein directed Battleship Potemkin and Alexander Nevsky.

clue.text: Enthusiastic about radical kind of blue prime minister

indicators.note: the keen word goes around the radical letter

parts.note: keen means enthusiastic
R is an abbreviation for radical
sky blue is a shade of blue

explanation.surface: A premier keen on a radical shade of Tory blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Kerensky headed Russia's Provisional Government in 1917.

clue.text: "We passed through a range of low arches, (…) and descending again, arrived at a deep -" (The Cask of Amontillado)

definitions.text: "We passed through a range of low arches, (…) and descending again, arrived at a deep -" (The Cask of Amontillado)

parts.words: "We passed through a range of low arches, (…) and descending again, arrived at a deep -" (The Cask of Amontillado)
parts.note: a quotation from Poe's tale with its last word replaced by a dash: the underground vault where the victim is walled up

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from Edgar Allan Poe's story.
explanation.definitionFit: Poe's narrator leads his victim down through catacombs to an underground burial vault.
